By BODMAS, 'of' means multiplication: $36 \div 6 = 6$ and '33 of 2' $= 66$.

$92 + 63 - 6 + 66 - 58 + 29 = 186$.

**Answer: 186**
questions.shortcut: Treat 'of' as x: 33 of 2 = 66, then add/subtract straight across.

Since $2 \times 4.25 \times 3.75 = 31.875$, the expression is of the form $a^2 + b^2 + 2ab$:

$(4.25 + 3.75)^2 = 8^2 = 64$.

**Answer: 64**

questions.q: The side of a square is 12 cm. What is the diagonal (in cm) of the square?
questions.solution:
Diagonal of a square of side $a$ is $a\sqrt{2}$.

Diagonal $= 12\sqrt{2}$ cm.

**Answer: $12\sqrt{2}$ cm**
questions.shortcut: Diagonal = side x root2 = 12 x 1.414 = 16.97 cm.

questions.q: The perimeter of a rhombus is 58 cm. One of the diagonal is 20 cm. What is the sum (in cm) of both the diagonals of the rhombus?
questions.solution:
Side $= \dfrac{58}{4} = 14.5$ cm. The half-diagonals and the side form a right triangle: one half-diagonal $= 10$, so the other $= \sqrt{14.5^2 - 10^2} = \sqrt{110.25} = 10.5$.

Second diagonal $= 21$ cm; sum of diagonals $= 20 + 21 = 41$ cm.

**Answer: 41**
questions.shortcut: Halves 10 and 10.5 with hypotenuse 14.5 are just the 20-21-29 triangle scaled by 1/2.

questions.q: Area of a rhombus is 840 square cm. Side of the rhombus is 37 cm. What is the sum (in cm) of its diagonals?
Highest Common Factor of A and B is 36 and C = 18. What is the Highest Common Factor of A, B and C?
questions.solution:
HCF(A, B, C) $=$ HCF of HCF(A, B) and C $=$ HCF(36, 18) $= 18$, since 36 is itself a multiple of 18.

**Answer: 18**
questions.shortcut: HCF(A,B) = 36 is a multiple of C = 18, so the common HCF is 18.

questions.q: The traffic lights at three different road crossings change after every 90 seconds, 120 seconds and 150 seconds respectively. If they all change simultaneously at 5:20 p.m., then find the time (in p.m.) at which they will change simultaneously again?
questions.solution:
They change together after LCM(90, 120, 150) seconds.
$90 = 2 \cdot 3^2 \cdot 5$, $120 = 2^3 \cdot 3 \cdot 5$, $150 = 2 \cdot 3 \cdot 5^2$ $\Rightarrow$ LCM $= 2^3 \cdot 3^2 \cdot 5^2 = 1800$ s $= 30$ min.

5:20 p.m. + 30 min $=$ 5:50 p.m.

**Answer: 5:50**

questions.q: A pipe can fill a tank in 100 minutes. In how much time (in seconds) can it fill 80 percent of the tank?
questions.solution:
Full tank takes 100 minutes, so 80% of the tank takes $0.8 \times 100 = 80$ min $= 80 \times 60 = 4800$ seconds.

**Answer: 4800**

questions.q: Q and R together are 3 times as efficient as P. P and R together are 2.5 times as efficient as Q. Q and R together can complete a work in 60 days. P alone can complete the same work in how many days?
questions.solution:
Efficiency-wise, $(Q + R) = 3P$. Since Q and R together finish the work in 60 days, P alone - one-third as efficient - takes $3 \times 60 = 180$ days. (The condition $P + R = 2.5\,Q$ is consistent with this but not needed.)

**Answer: 180**
questions.shortcut: P is 1/3 as efficient as (Q + R), so P's time = 3 x 60 = 180 days.

questions.q: The speed of a train is 20 km/hr. Length of the train is 450 metres. How much time (in minutes) the train will take to cross a man standing on the platform?
questions.solution:
Speed $= 20$ km/h $= 20 \times \dfrac{5}{18} = \dfrac{50}{9}$ m/s.

Time to cross a man $= \dfrac{450}{50/9} = 81$ s $= \dfrac{81}{60} = \dfrac{27}{20}$ min.

**Answer: $\dfrac{27}{20}$ minutes**
questions.shortcut: t(s) = 3.6 x length/speed(km/h) = 3.6 x 450/20 = 81 s = 27/20 min.

questions.q: The speed of a train is 40 km/hr. Length of the train is 500 metres. How much time (in minutes) the train will take to cross a man standing on the platform?
questions.solution:
Speed $= 40$ km/h $= \dfrac{100}{9}$ m/s.

Time $= \dfrac{500}{100/9} = 45$ s $= \dfrac{45}{60} = \dfrac{3}{4}$ min.

**Answer: $\dfrac{3}{4}$ minutes**

questions.q: If p-q : q-r : r-s = 3 : 4 : 7, then what is the value of (p+s) : r?
questions.solution:
Let $p - q = 3k$, $q - r = 4k$, $r - s = 7k$.
Then $p - r = 3k + 4k = 7k \Rightarrow p = r + 7k$, and $s = r - 7k$.
So $p + s = (r + 7k) + (r - 7k) = 2r$.

$(p + s) : r = 2 : 1$.

**Answer: 2 : 1**
questions.shortcut: p - r = 7k and r - s = 7k, so p + s = 2r.

questions.q: The ratio of two number A and B is 3 : 1. If both numbers are increased by 2, then the ratio of A and B becomes 5 : 3. What is the sum of initial values of A and B?
questions.solution:
Let $A = 3x$, $B = x$. After adding 2: $\dfrac{3x + 2}{x + 2} = \dfrac{5}{3} \Rightarrow 9x + 6 = 5x + 10 \Rightarrow 4x = 4 \Rightarrow x = 1$.

Initial sum $= A + B = 4x = 4$.

**Answer: 4**
questions.shortcut: 3x : x with +2 each gives 5 : 3; try x = 1 -> A = 3, B = 1, sum = 4.

questions.q: The marked price of an article is (7/5) of the cost price. Its selling price is (6/7) of the marked price. What is the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
SP $= \dfrac{6}{7} \times$ MP $= \dfrac{6}{7} \times \dfrac{7}{5} \times$ CP $= \dfrac{6}{5}\,\text{CP}$.

Profit $= \dfrac{1}{5}$ of CP $= 20\%$.

**Answer: 20 percent**

questions.q: Which of the following will have the highest selling price?
options: Marked price = Rs. 8000 and Discount = 25 percent
Marked price = Rs. 6000 and Discount = 25 percent
Marked price = Rs. 5000 and Discount = 30 percent
Marked price = Rs. 8000 and Discount = 30 percent
questions.solution:
SP $=$ MP $\times (1 - \text{discount})$:
(a) $8000 \times 0.75 = 6000$; (b) $6000 \times 0.75 = 4500$; (c) $5000 \times 0.70 = 3500$; (d) $8000 \times 0.70 = 5600$.

The highest SP is Rs. 6000.

**Answer: Marked price = Rs. 8000 and Discount = 25 percent**

questions.q: Which of the following will have marked price Rs. 4000?
options: Selling price = Rs. 3000 and Discount = 25 percent
Selling price = Rs. 2500 and Discount = 15 percent
Selling price = Rs. 3800 and Discount = 12 percent
Selling price = Rs. 3200 and Discount = 15 percent
questions.solution:
MP $= \dfrac{\text{SP}}{1 - \text{discount}}$:
(a) $\dfrac{3000}{0.75} = 4000$; (b) $\dfrac{2500}{0.85} \approx 2941$; (c) $\dfrac{3800}{0.88} \approx 4318$; (d) $\dfrac{3200}{0.85} \approx 3765$.

Only option (a) gives exactly Rs. 4000.

**Answer: Selling price = Rs. 3000 and Discount = 25 percent**
questions.shortcut: 25% discount means MP = SP x 4/3 = 3000 x 4/3 = 4000.

questions.q: What is the fourth proportion of 12, 4 and 18?
questions.solution:
Fourth proportional $x$ to 12, 4, 18 satisfies $\dfrac{12}{4} = \dfrac{18}{x}$.

$x = \dfrac{4 \times 18}{12} = 6$.

**Answer: 6**
